children: Indonesia's current account deficit narrowed significantly to 0.5% of gross domestic product in the third quarter, compared with a revised deficit of 3.4% of GDP in the previous three months, central bank data showed on Friday.
Its balance of payments recorded a surplus of $80 million in the third quarter, a swing from the $882 million deficit in the second quarter

The balance of payments surplus was mainly supported by a narrowing current account deficit amid a higher surplus in the non-oil and gas goods trade balance and a lower deficit in the oil and gas trade balance, the central bank added
The narrower current account deficit of $2 billion was driven by higher non-oil and gas exports amid rising prices of Indonesia's export commodities and lower energy imports

Indonesia's current account position is closely watched by investors and policymakers and often seen as an indicator of economic vulnerability, with the country exposed to capital outflows and weighing on the rupiah, which earlier this week hit another record low
Going forward, Bank Indonesia expects the balance of payments to remain favorable to support external resilience
It projects the current account deficit to remain low through improved exports and rising global commodity prices
